name: Enfortumab vedotin + Pembrolizumab (EV-302)

biomarkers.note: Enfortumab vedotin (Nectin-4-directed antibody-drug conjugate) + pembrolizumab (anti-PD-1). Preferred first-line systemic therapy for locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma (bladder #57, upper-tract #58); no positive companion biomarker is required (PD-L1 not required). EV-302 established superiority over platinum-based chemotherapy. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Bladder Cancer v3.2026 (BL-G); DeVita 12th ed. (Pembrolizumab plus enfortumab vedotin as preferred first-line).

lineOfTherapy: first-line (preferred) for locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma, first-line
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v3.2026, BL-G (Enfortumab vedotin + Pembrolizumab, preferred first-line; references 13, 14, 44)

drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., line 58568: pembrolizumab 200 mg flat dose IV, day 1 every 3 weeks (standard flat dose; alternative 400 mg every 6 weeks per label). Immune-related adverse event monitoring applies.

drugs.notes: The 1.25 mg/kg IV dose value is grounded to DeVita 12th ed., line 20821-20827 (the enfortumab vedotin monotherapy dosing table). The EV-302 combination schedule (days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle) is combo-specific and is NOT printed in the provided licensed sources, so the days and cycleLengthDays stay VERIFY (never invented) and must be resolved against a cited source before use. EV-specific safety (hyperglycemia, peripheral neuropathy, severe skin reactions including SJS/TEN, ocular) applies.

supportiveCare: Immune-related adverse event (irAE) monitoring for pembrolizumab (thyroid and other endocrinopathies, hepatitis, colitis, pneumonitis, dermatitis, nephritis).
Enfortumab vedotin HYPERGLYCEMIA: monitor blood glucose before dosing; risk of serious/fatal diabetic ketoacidosis.
Enfortumab vedotin PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY: assess before each dose; can be dose-limiting.
Enfortumab vedotin SKIN REACTIONS: monitor for severe cutaneous reactions including Stevens-Johnson syndrome / toxic epidermal necrolysis (SJS/TEN).
Enfortumab vedotin OCULAR toxicity: prophylactic artificial tears; ophthalmology for symptoms.
Overlapping skin toxicity between EV and pembrolizumab requires careful attribution.

monitoring: immune-related toxicity screen (TSH/free T4, LFTs, glucose, cortisol) during pembrolizumab
blood glucose before each EV dose (hyperglycemia / DKA)
skin assessment for severe cutaneous reactions (SJS/TEN)

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 2 or higher immune-related adverse event
doseModificationRules.text: Hold pembrolizumab and manage with corticosteroids per immune-related adverse event guidance; obtain clinical review before rechallenge.

doseModificationRules.condition: hyperglycemia, grade 2+ neuropathy, or severe skin reaction
doseModificationRules.text: Hold enfortumab vedotin for hyperglycemia (blood glucose > 250 mg/dL); hold/reduce for grade 2 or higher neuropathy; permanently discontinue for grade 3-4 or suspected SJS/TEN skin reactions. Dose modification cannot be finalized until the EV starting dose (VERIFY) is resolved.

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab (EV-302) as preferred first-line therapy for locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma (bladder #57, upper-tract #58). Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks is sourced to DeVita 12th ed., line 58568. The enfortumab vedotin 1.25 mg/kg IV value is grounded to DeVita 12th ed., line 20821-20827 (the enfortumab vedotin monotherapy dosing table); the EV-302 combination schedule (days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle) is combo-specific and is NOT printed in the provided licensed sources, so the days and cycleLengthDays stay VERIFY and are never inferred (verifyFields records the schedule paths). Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Bladder Cancer v3.2026 (BL-G) establish EV + pembrolizumab as a preferred first-line regimen. Both immune-related (pembrolizumab) and enfortumab-vedotin-specific (hyperglycemia, neuropathy, SJS/TEN skin reactions, ocular) safety are captured. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
